top.title: Glenn Schumann is set to be FSU football's next coach. What's his recruiting track record?
top.description: It turns out the man partially responsible for the beginning of Mike Norvell's downfall is set to become Florida State 's next football coach. Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann is expected to be named Florida State's next head football coach , USA TODAY Sports John Brice reported Monday, Nov. 23. The Glenn Schumann-coached Georgia defense coasted to a 63-3 win over the Seminoles in the 2023 Orange Bowl on Dec. 30, 2023. Just more that 1,000 days later, Schumann is set to replace Norvell, who was fired on Nov. 1. Schumann, 36, did not play college football, but enrolled at Alabama to work under legendary head coach Nick Saban in 2008. He worked in various roles under Saban and then-defensive coordinator Kirby Smart before following Smart to Athens, Georgia, as the inside linebackers coach in 2016. Schumann was promoted to co-defensive coordinator with now-Oregon coach Dan Lanning in 2019 and then served as co-defensive coordinator with Will Muschamp before being promoted to the full-time role in 2024, shortly after the blowout win vs. FSU. After the struggles Norvell had as a recruiter with the Seminoles , FSU fans may wonder about Schumann's experience and track record on the recruiting trail. Well, Schumann has helped the Bulldogs sign 14 five-stars during his time with the program. Here is a look at the five best players Schumann served as a primary recruiter for: Raylen Wilson, 5-star linebacker (2023) Schumann hails from Valdosta, Georgia. That being only about 75 miles northeast of Tallahassee, Florida, helped his connection with Wilson, the No. 28 overall player in the 2023 recruiting cycle. The relationship between Schumann and Wilson helped the Bulldogs pluck Wilson from Lincoln High School in Tallahassee to and send him to Athens instead of staying home with the Seminoles. Remember, at this time, FSU and Norvell were riding the high of coming off a 10-3 season. While Wilson is not the highest-ranked recruit Schumann added in his time at Georgia, he's been productive for the Bulldogs, tallying 102 career tackles, 8.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and an interception. Now the head coach at Florida State, keeping those relationships with Tallahassee-area programs will be key for Schumann. Nolan Smith, 5-star edge rusher (2019) The former five-star recruit out of IMG Academy (Bradenton, FL) lived up to expectations as the No. 1 overall player — according to 247Sports Composite rankings — in the 2019 recruiting cycle. Schumann played the primary recruiting role for Smith, who now plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, in his first recruiting cycle with the Bulldogs. Smith finished with 114 total tackles, 21 tackles for loss and 11.5 sacks in his time in Athens. Following four years with the Bulldogs — a span that included two national championships — Smith was the No. 30 overall pick by the Eagles in 2023 NFL Draft. top.title: 2027 Five-star CJ Rosser commits to UNC
top.description: Clarence CJ Rosser Jr., #14 of the United States of America (USA) in action during the FIBA U17 Basketball World Cup - Turkiye 2026 Group A match between the United States of America (USA) and France at Basketball Development Centre in Istanbul, Turkey on June 27, 2026. (Photo by Altan Gocher / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images) | Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images Today it was announced that 2027 five-star power forward CJ Rosser has committed to the University of North Carolina. This announcement is the second that Michael Malone has earned from the 2027 class so far, and it has given the Tar Heels potentially their best recruiting class in over a decade. Breaking: CJ Rosser, the No. 3 ranked player in the SC Next 100 for the Class of 2027, has committed to North Carolina, he announced. pic.twitter.com/M4AjKwhi4U — SportsCenter NEXT (@SCNext) November 23, 2026 There was a lot of speculation that Rosser was ready to announce his commitment, but the signs weren’t particularly clear. He had canceled an official visit to Kentucky, and around that time On3’s Joe Tipton had changed his crystal ball to favor the Tar Heels. Rosser is a 6’10, 200-lb power forward from Orlando, FL. He currently players for Southeastern Prep, and he is considered the second-best player in the country according to the 247Sports Composite Rankings . Rosser chose the Tar Heels over Miami, NC State, Arkansas, Kentucky, USC, and Louisville. Scouting reports indicate that Rosser is an inside-out player that has a lot of athleticism and defensive potential. It’s fair to say that some of the things being said about him aren’t far off from what we heard about Caleb Wilson, which is that he’s an inside-out player that is still kind of raw but has a lot of upside. Social media has been calling Rosser “Baby KD,” referring to current Houston Rockets star, Kevin Durant. Checking out some of his moves on the court paints a pretty vivid picture as to why he earned the moniker. View Link This is incredible news for Michael Malone and his staff, and for the Carolina fan base as a whole. The Heels have now earned commitments from two top-five players, one of whom has officially signed in Demarcus Henry. The best part is that Malone still isn’t finished — word on the street is that UNC is still in play for Beckham Black, and Jalen Davis, who currently has UNC in his top four, plans to announce where he is attending school tomorrow. There’s a lot more actively going on with Malone’s recruiting board, but ultimately this was the best news that could’ve been delivered right before UNC’s game against Monmouth. top.title: Tigers Emerge as Potential Landing Spot for Former All-Star Pitcher
top.description: The Detroit Tigers may have another intriguing name to consider as they look to strengthen their starting rotation for the 2027 season. According to MLB Network insider Jon Paul Morosi, former Kansas City Royals All-Star Kris Bubic is among the free-agent pitchers who could make sense for Detroit this offseason. The 29-year-old left-hander is coming off a season that included a trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers, an injury-related absence, and a return in time for postseason action. Now a free agent, Bubic could represent an opportunity for Tigers president of baseball operations Scott Harris to add a pitcher with considerable upside without necessarily committing to a lengthy contract. Oct 4, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) reacts after being relieved during the fifth inning against the Atlanta Braves in game two of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) MLB Insider Names Tigers as Potential Kris Bubic Destination During a November 18 appearance on MLB Network, Morosi discussed Bubic’s free-agent market and identified Detroit as one of several potential landing spots. His comments, also highlighted by MLB.com’s November 19 rumor roundup , suggest the Tigers could be an appealing destination for the former Royals standout. “So again, teams like the Royals who know him well, the Tigers who would like to get a shorter-term starting pitcher, Cubs, Orioles, [Blue] Jays, and the Cardinals as well,” Morosi explained. That is an interesting development for Detroit, especially considering the organization’s need for additional pitching depth. However, it is important to distinguish Morosi identifying the Tigers as a potential fit from a report confirming that Harris has entered negotiations with Bubic. Detroit has already been connected to other free-agent starting pitchers, including former Chicago Cubs All-Star Shota Imanaga . Adding Bubic to the discussion gives Tigers fans another name to monitor as the club attempts to put together a more dependable rotation. What Kris Bubic Could Bring to Detroit Bubic’s appeal begins with his ability to perform at a high level when healthy. During the 2025 season with Kansas City, he earned his first American League All-Star selection after posting an impressive 2.55 ERA across 20 starts and 116⅓ innings. His success was not limited to that one season, either, as MLB.com’s examination of his free-agent market noted that Bubic has recorded a 2.90 ERA over the past three seasons while working in both starting and relief roles. That performance makes him an intriguing candidate for teams seeking upside in the free-agent market. However, durability remains a legitimate concern. top.title: Fernando Mendoza gave Raiders a glimpse of their future with ownership after loss
top.description: Alex Singleton had spent Sunday afternoon trying to make Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL road start as miserable as possible. By the time it was over, the Broncos linebacker sounded like a man who understood Denver had better enjoy days like this against the Raiders quarterback while it could. “He’s a first-round pick, first overall for a reason,” Singleton said. “He’s going to be a good player.” And that was after the Broncos tagged Mendoza for five sacks. Imagine what Singleton might say someday when the kid has time to throw. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) throws against the Denver Broncos in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Jack Dempsey Mendoza earned the compliment. Playing without Brock Bowers, his best receiver, in a stadium loud enough to cost the Raiders an early timeout, he threw three touchdown passes. Patrick Mahomes is the only other visiting quarterback to do that in Denver this season. Matthew Stafford managed two. Sam Darnold and Trevor Lawrence left town without one between them. Mendoza also joined Lawrence and Joe Burrow as the only quarterbacks drafted first overall to throw for at least 250 yards and three touchdowns in a game within their first two career starts. Somewhere down the line, maybe Mendoza will appreciate the company he kept Sunday. In Denver, he seemed more interested in a cornerback named Ja’Quan McMillian. And that might be the best news the Raiders brought home. “Don’t get me wrong, although I believe it was an improvement, there are a lot of things I need to improve on for next week,” Mendoza said. Denver Broncos’ Alex Singleton (49) sacks Las Vegas Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza (15) during a game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images Take the throw that McMillian returned for a touchdown. If you want to understand the distance Mendoza traveled in a week and how much ground he still has to cover, listen to him explain what happened in the instant before he let that ball go. “I saw him take a shuffle inside – thought he was walling another slant – and I let it go with anticipation, and he made a fantastic play,” Mendoza said. A week earlier against Seattle, Mendoza was trying to see the entire field. In Denver, he picked up a cornerback shuffling inside, understood what that movement usually meant for a different receiver, and threw to the spot he expected to come open. McMillian got a hand on the ball. All that processing, and the guy who wound up in the end zone played for Denver. The easy thing would have been to tip his cap and leave it there. Mendoza was considering what a checkdown over the middle might have bought him. A few yards. Another down. A chance for his defense to catch its breath. top.title: Texas defensive back Kobe Black out for rest of season with knee injury but Hero Kanu could return
top.description: Texas defensive back Kobe Black (6) is out for the rest of the season with a knee injury. (Jason Fochtman/Staff photographer) AUSTIN - Texas safety Kobe Black has been ruled out for the rest of the season, but defensive tackle Hero Kanu could possibly return to the team in the playoffs after his arm surgery a week ago, Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. Asked if there's any chance Kanu could get back after surgery for a torn biceps, Sarkisian smiled and said, "Potentially. I'll use that word." Black, who was moved from cornerback in the offseason and played 341 snaps, left Saturday's game against Arkansas early with a knee injury. His absence will deprive Texas of one of its top backups. "I hate it for him," Sarkisian said. "It's disappointing. He was having a really good year for us with the position change. But the other guys need to step up." top.title: Boston Celtics at Washington Wizards: Stream, lineups, injury reports, broadcast (11/24)
top.description: The NBA regular season can be like a roller coaster. The Boston Celtics currently find themselves on the part of the ride that points straight down — except there's no fun in this steep drop. The C's have lost four games in a row, which is enough for their longest losing streak since the 2020-21 campaign. They'll look for a reprieve in the regular-season roller coaster on Tuesday night, when they face the Washington Wizards in D.C. It's no secret that the Celtics have had the Wizards' number in recent years. They've beat their Eastern Conference foe 11 consecutive times, with the last win for the Wizards dating back to March of 2023. But, these aren't the same Wiz the C's have crushed in the past. Washington has prevailed in three straight contests after a slow start to the season and seems to have found a stud in forward AJ Dybantsa, the first overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft (and a former Celtics fan who grew up less than an hour outside of Boston). Meanwhile, the Celtics are reeling and need to play desperate in the nation's capital to avoid going 0-4 on their rough road trip. Records, standing, and streaks The Celtics have lost four games in a row and, for the moment, sit in third place in the Eastern Conference with an 11-6 record. The Wizards have won three games in a row and own a 7-11 record. They're just barely in Play-In Tournament territory, as they hold ninth place in the East. Player injuries For the third consecutive night, Celtics center Mitchell Robinson is out with an illness. As for the Wizards, Reece Beekman (right AC joint sprain), Justin Champagnie (right foot surgery), Tristan Vukcevic (left hip impingement), and Jamir Watkins (left ACL repair) are out on Tuesday evening. Two-way center Felix Okpara is listed as questionable. top.description: The Los Angeles Rams could be in for a rude awakening for their Thanksgiving Eve game against the Green Bay Packers. With the game set to kick off on Wednesday night, teams sent in their final injury reports and the Packers revealed that edge rusher Micah Parsons will be making his season debut against the Rams. Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons speaks with Los Angeles Dodgers staff members before a game at Dodger Stadium on Monday, April 27, 2026. Kevork Djansezian for CA Post It’s been nearly 12 months since Parsons tore his left ACL against the Denver Broncos in December of last season, and the three-time All-Pro has been steadily working his way back by thoroughly rehabbing his injured knee. Since his rookie debut in 2021, Parsons has been a force to be reckoned with on opposing offensive lines, with five consecutive seasons where he registered over 12 sacks. Parsons’ highest number of sacks in a season came in 2023, when he tallied 14 for the Dallas Cowboys. After a contract dispute just before the 2025 NFL season began, Parsons was traded from Dallas to Green Bay in exchange for a first-round pick in 2026 and 2027, as well as defensive tackle Kenny Clark. Rams offensive lineman Dylan McMahon walking off the field against the Cardinals. Getty Images Before his injury last year, Parsons had 12.5 through 14 games, and won 23 percent of his pass rushes, finishing the year third behind Nik Bonito and Nick Herbig. Parsons will likely be monitored on how many snaps he appears in, but for the Rams, his return comes at an inconvenient time, as the team lost starting and backup centers, Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon — both of whom are on the team’s injured reserve. Arizona Cardinals linebacker Zaven Collins (25) sacks Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) in Glendale, Ariz., Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin With the two out, Beaux Limmer, who was filling in for Steve Avila at left guard, was moved to center during the Rams’ Week 10 game against the Cardinals. Ironically, the Rams got their running game going in the second half when Limmer moved over, and finished the game running for 202 yards and were led by Blake Corum who had 17 carries for 100 yards and a touchdown.

top.title: North Carolina TE Jelani Thurman gives away 45 turkeys before Thanksgiving, pays tribute to late mom
top.description: North Carolina tight end Jelani Thurman is honoring his late mother, former WNBA All-Star Kara Braxton , this Thanksgiving holiday. The Carolina star gave away 45 turkeys ahead of the big day Thursday, honoring his mother’s old jersey number. Braxton wore No. 45 with all three WNBA organizations she played for (Detroit/Tulsa Shock, Phoenix Mercury, and New York Liberty) over the course of her nine-year professional career. Braxton, who was just 43 years old, passed away in February following a tragic car accident. Her son, Thurman, is in the midst of his fourth collegiate football season (his first at North Carolina ). The Fairburn, Ga. native is enjoying a career-best campaign, as he’s hauled in 51 catches for 610 yards and eight scores this season. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “She taught me to always go hard. There’s one goal. You know what you need to do,” Thurman said earlier this year , when asked about advice his mom would give him. Honestly, with her going to a championship, she told me about some of the experiences she had and some of the things she had to do to get there. Photos courtesy of David Ben-Zaken With one regular season game remaining, Thurman is second on his team in receiving yards, and leads the team with eight touchdowns. No other Carolina receiver has hauled in more than three touchdowns this season. North Carolina heads into its regular season finale with a 5-6 (2-5) record, needing a win over rival NC State to clinch bowl eligibility for the first time under head coach Bill Belichick. Thanksgiving is bring best out of college football players Thurman isn’t the only college football player giving back this Thanksgiving. Florida WR Vernell Brown III also gave away turkeys to families ahead of the holiday in partnership with his VB3 Family Foundation . Sunday afternoon, Brown gave away 100 turkey dinners ahead of the holiday at an event at the Martin Luther King Jr. Multipurpose Center. The event was due to run for two hours, but 100 families claimed the turkeys in just 13 minutes, according to the Gainesville Sun . top.title: Urban Meyer says Jeremiah Smith may be best college football player ever
top.description: It's no surprise that former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer picked Ohio State to beat Michigan in the upcoming rivalry game on Nov. 28. While Meyer picked the Michigan defense as the best unit on the field, he had glowing words to say about Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. "On offense, we've got the best player in the country, maybe the best player ever to play college football. That's how good Jeremiah [Smith] is," Meyer said to 10TV . "But we also have a backup quarterback. And the offensive line's not playing great." Meyer predicted a low-scoring "rock fight" between the two likely non-playoff teams because of the strengths in Michigan's defense and Ohio State's offense. "I think this is going to be a rock fight, whoever punches the hardest is going to win" Urban Meyer says OSU has the more talented roster, but Michigan's defense is the best unit. He added Jeremiah Smith might be the best player to ever play college football, he is picking OSU: pic.twitter.com/7cnrwI1weT — Adam King (@AdamKing10TV) November 22, 2026 "The roster's better at Ohio State ... the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense, and that concerns me a little bit. They really hammered UCLA," Meyer said. "You've got to think: the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible ... they kept UCLA to three points until right near the end of the game, so that's a legit defense." Michigan upset UCLA with a 18-16 triple overtime victory on Nov. 21. Michigan's offense has been stagnant for most of the season, ranking 132nd in the FBS in yards per game and 129th in points per game. Bryce Underwood, who was benched earlier in the season, is expected to start against Ohio State. He went 8 for 18 for 63 yards and an interception against Ohio State in 2025. Ohio State will be entering the rivalry game with a loss as its latest result. The Buckeyes fell 31-28 to Nebraska and struggled defensively, allowing 30-plus points for the third time in the last four games. Smith had 165 receiving yards and two touchdowns against Nebraska. He leads the FBS in receiving yards and touchdowns. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Urban Meyer says Jeremiah Smith may be best college football player ever

top.title: Vegas is the center of the sports world right now. Why is everyone so mad about it?
top.description: Nov 16, 2023; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; The MSG Sphere is observed prior to the start of the first at Formula 1 Heineken Silver Las Vegas Grand Prix practice at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Las Vegas often finds itself at the center of the sports universe, but the last two weeks of November have become among the most vital on Southern Nevada’s civic calendar with the presence of F1 and college basketball’s Players Era Festival both being held on the Strip. On Saturday night, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won his third Las Vegas Grand Prix in four years, claiming a race that’s gotten consensus rave reviews and is being hailed as one of the sport’s all-time classics. Verstappen, ever the showman, followed it up with a hilarious tirade against rival George Russell, who dared to engage in a war of words with motorsport’s pettiest man. Exactly 48 hours before lights went out at the Grand Prix, Houston and Kansas tipped off in the championship game of the Players Era 8, the first of two college hoops “festivals” occurring before and during the patented “Feast Week”. Houston held on for a 86-76 win, and it was an especially meaningful result because it was the culmination of a career defining week for Cougars point guard and Las Vegas native Dedan Thomas Jr., who became the city’s most popular hooper in a generation during his time at Liberty and the two years he spent at UNLV. The Players Era 16 is set to tip-off on Tuesday, featuring twice as many teams as the Players Era 8 did (yes, that’s what the numbers mean). This week’s bracket doesn’t feature the at-the-time top ranked team in Florida and the top-ranked prospect in Kansas’ Tyran Stokes like last week’s did, but it’s still an exceptionally strong field with contenders like Gonzaga, Louisville, St. John’s and Texas Tech. Not without controversy Like most things that have to do with the City of Sin, however, both the Grand Prix and the hoops tournament have taken their fair share of criticism in the short time they’ve been present. We could talk for years about the saga F1 officials have put Las Vegas locals through since 2023, from the lost profits blocked businesses suffer during construction and race weekend, to the Los Angeles-esque traffic on the Strip when the streets are shut down. Among F1’s global fanbase and even its drivers, the race is viewed as much as a PR event as it is a motorsports contest, although the quality of racing has removed all doubt that it’s ultimately a net positive. The Players Era discourse has occurred strictly on a national scale, as the tournament has been getting pelted with proverbial tomatoes because it’s seen by fans as yet another relic of what feels more and more like the twilight of collegiate sports. top.description: Tyson Fury attends a press conference Sept. 30 in London ahead of his upcoming fight with Anthony Joshua. (Kin Cheung / Associated Press) In late 2015, Tyson Fury had everything he had every wanted. He was happily married, starting a family and was the unified world heavyweight champion. But everything unraveled quickly for the boxer from Manchester, England. He started abusing alcohol and drugs. His weight skyrocketed to nearly 400 pounds. He was declared medically unfit to box. And he didn’t care. “I didn’t care about myself, my health, my family, my wife, my kids, nothing,” Fury said in the Netflix documentary “Tyson Fury,” which premieres Friday. “Belts, boxing, money, nothing mattered. ... Only self-destruct. That’s what mattered.” Read more: UFC's Tommy McMillen says recent overdose was 'eye-opener,' but he's not going to stop partying 'cold turkey' After a severe anxiety attack in 2016, Fury said, he visited a psychiatrist, who said he “ticked all the boxes” for a number of disorders, including depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder. His wife, Paris Fury, said in the documentary that the psychiatrist also told them that Fury is “a mild schizophrenic.” “It was like, don’t be silly. What’s she on about, schizophrenic?” Paris Fury said. “Maniacs are schizophrenic. You’re not schizophrenic. I had never heard of bipolar. What’s bipolar? When somebody actually explained it to me … I was like, wow, that’s him to a T.” As an undefeated young boxer, Fury had his sights set on claiming the unified heavyweight title from Wladimir Klitschko , who had held the belts since 2008. In November 2015, he did just that, upsetting the Ukranian boxer by unanimous decision — almost immediately afterward, Fury’s inner struggles started to surface. “I achieved all my childhood dreams,” Fury said. “Focused on this one man throughout my full career, the man no one could beat. And then when I finally beat this man, it was like my whole point of existence had been taken away.” Fury said he started hearing constant voices in his head, often telling him to harm himself. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” Fury said. “I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. top.description: Utah running back Wayshawn Parker (1) runs the ball during the first half of an NCAA college football game against Cincinnati, Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in Cincinnati. | Tony Wagner, Associated Press In each of Utah’s last two games, running back Wayshawn Parker has played in one series before heading to the sidelines for the rest of the game. Utah’s star running back has been dealing with a heel bruise that he suffered early in the BYU game. In the two games since, Parker has attempted to play, but the pain has been too great for him to continue. Parker practiced ahead of Utah’s win at TCU, warmed up and led the team in his customary “wake up” chant ahead of the contest in Fort Worth. But after one carry, Parker limped off the field and eventually watched the rest of the game in street clothes. “This week we had a little bit more, not a little bit, we had much more practice time with him — so the ability to cut and do some of the things that he would’ve been doing on game day. It happened that in this warmup, he just felt a different type of pain,” Scalley said. Parker did not worsen the existing injury, Scalley said. “It ends up being not any more significant of injury. He didn’t worsen the issue, so that’s good. But we just did not, at that point, want to do anything that would keep him from further football this season,” Scalley said. Parker has been a huge piece of Utah’s offense, rushing for 765 yards and nine touchdowns on 125 carries. He’s added 269 receiving yards and four touchdowns and has been a big plus in pass blocking, something that has been glaring in his absence in the last two games. Parker’s status for this week’s game will become more clear as Friday approaches, but it wouldn’t be a big surprise if Utah rests him. top.title: ‘As poor as it gets’ – Weather fears for Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs game on Thanksgiving
top.description: Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images A perfect night of viewing for NFL fans on Thanksgiving could only be ruined by the weather at Highmark Stadium. The late Thanksgiving game between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs could be impacted by the weather, according to latest forecasts. Local Buffalo reporter Jon Scott of the WGRZ station reports: “Just told by our @WGRZ weather folks that conditions for #Bills and Chiefs on Thanksgiving night are going to be about as poor as it gets. “Steady rain and upper 30s before, during, and after the game.” Weather forecast is ‘rain’ for Buffalo vs Chiefs The National Weather Service forecasts 100 percent chance of rain on Thanksgiving night, with a temperature of around 36 degrees. A 10 mph wind speed is also being forecast, to mix in with the rainy and cold conditions. The inclement weather will have an impact on the fans in attendance, in addition to the players – although the Highmark Stadium roof will offer some protection. The curved canopy covers around 65 percent of the stadium, in contrast with the Bills’ previous arena, where the entire stadium was open to the elements. Unfortunately for the players and the turf, the open-air field will still bear the brunt of the downpour. The Chiefs are 8-2 heading in to play the Bills, who are 9-1 and top of the AFC. Fans in Buffalo are used to bad weather, with infamous snow games in the past. And while those games can be a lot of fun for viewers at home – they are tough for attending fans. Rainy weather can be grim all around. The conditions rarely make for peak football conditions, and the game could really put the two teams’ elite running games to the test. James Cook has more than 1,000 scrimmage yards, as does Kenneth Walker for the Chiefs, if he is healthy enough to play. Emmett Johnson has filled in impressively in his absence. top.title: How Did Sea Lions’ “Arf Arf” Chant Originate?
top.description: At the end of the San Jose Sea Lions’ first practice, players gathered in a circle near center ice and, on the count of three, shouted, “Let’s go, Sea Lions!” Then they started barking. Ending practice with arf arf arf🦭🦭 pic.twitter.com/eJ5pbvnDKQ — Eli Fastiff (@Eli_Fastiff) November 20, 2026 “It happened organically, immediately after all the branding came out, just to add a little fun to practice,” said rookie goaltender Tia Chan when asked about the arf-arf-arfing. “Hopefully the fans get behind it.” The attempted imitation of San Jose’s sea lion mascot isn’t surprising to those inside the expansion team’s locker room. It also doesn’t hurt that multiple players made stops at Pier 39 in San Francisco to promote the team’s branding on social media. View this post on Instagram “I think it was just we’ve got a lot of funny people on our team, and I think … you find out that you’re a sea lion and stuff just comes out, I guess,” said forward Maddi Wheeler. “But whether it’s on purpose or on accident, I think it’s just a pretty funny thing. It’s very lighthearted in the room. We’re all excited to be here, so it’s just a fun little thing.” Speaking to reporters after the team’s second practice, rookie forward Sloane Matthews echoed Wheeler’s assessment. “I think we have a lot of energy; everyone is getting along in the locker room,” Matthews said. “We’re all making jokes, laughing. So it’s kind of a lot of lightheartedness and just getting to know each other, just figuring it out.” That upbeat Sea Jose Sea Lions locker-room vibe has helped the new team quickly build its culture. “I’m having a lot of fun already; it’s a lot of great people,” Wheeler said. “I think we’re all very committed to building a strong culture. We’ve been here for half a week, and it’s already set in.” Head Coach-GM Troy Ryan has noticed his team bonding quickly. For example, when asked about rookie forward Lily Shannon, the first thing Ryan mentioned was that she and Chan hosted the team for dinner this weekend. “Sometimes that’s not what you get from first-year players,” Ryan said. The team will gather again for lunch on Thursday to celebrate Thanksgiving. “It’s nice because … we got a good mix of Americans, Canadians, and actually quite a few internationals,” Wheeler said. “Whenever you can connect off the ice, it’s going to help build your team culture.” So far, that culture is at its loudest when the San Jose Sea Lions end practice. “I think the girls are leaning into it. I think, you know, it’s a fun thing,” said forward Justine Reyes. “Like, might as well. nigeria.title: FG seeks stronger food policies to curb malnutrition, NCDs
nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has called for stronger implementation of healthy food policies to address malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and the rising burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, made the call on Monday while delivering the keynote address at the maiden National Healthy Food Week and Learning Conference 2026 in Abuja. The conference, themed, “Our Food, Our Health, Our Future,” was organised to promote healthier food systems and strengthen efforts to address nutrition-related health challenges. Represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Ms. Daju Kachollom, Salako said tackling the country’s nutrition and health challenges required stronger collaboration among government institutions, regulatory agencies, food manufacturers, health professionals, researchers, development partners, the media and consumers. He noted that food choices and the quality of food available in markets, schools, hospitals, workplaces and homes had significant implications for public health, workforce productivity, child development and national prosperity. The minister said the Federal Government had introduced several policies and regulatory measures to improve food safety and nutritional standards, including the Revised National Policy on Food Safety and Quality and its Implementation Plan (2023). He said the policy framework promoted food safety, food fortification, sodium reduction, elimination of industrially produced trans fats and healthier food procurement practices in public institutions. Salako also highlighted the National Guidelines for Sodium Reduction, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control’s (NAFDAC) Read the Label Campaign and the development of front-of-pack nutrition labelling as measures to help consumers make informed food choices and encourage manufacturers to improve the nutritional quality of their products. On public food procurement, he said government institutions provided millions of meals annually through schools, hospitals, correctional centres, emergency shelters and National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) camps, making public procurement an important instrument for improving the country’s food environment. He urged relevant authorities to ensure effective implementation of the Bureau of Public Procurement’s National Guidelines for Public Procurement of Food and Related Services through adequate monitoring, accountability and capacity building. The minister also identified fiscal measures, including the sugar-sweetened beverage tax, as important tools for discouraging excessive consumption of sugary drinks and generating revenue for public health interventions. He advocated transparent allocation of part of the revenue to nutrition education, healthier food environments and the prevention of diet-related diseases. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks. Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN. According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027. He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation. The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious. He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine. Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026. On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres. He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said. He then asked the NUC for support in four areas: the timely nomination of academic staff of verified non-partisan standing, the alignment of academic calendars with the election dates, collaboration on voter education and counter-disinformation on campuses, and the welfare and recognition of academics deployed for election duty. nigeria.description: *Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) and Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023. The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years. More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic. nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed. The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Executive Council and the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council paid separate condolence visits to the Governor’s family at the Government House, Jos. The Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, who led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the Governor’s Residence at the Old Government House, Jos, described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian who made meaningful contributions to public service.” She said the Council received the news of his passing “with profound shock and sadness,” noting that his death was “not only a painful loss to the Mutfwang family but also a significant loss to Plateau State and the nation, given his contributions to society and his exemplary life.” Piyo prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise “the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss.” In a separate visit, the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also condoled with the Governor and his family over the death of Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang. The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji (Dr.) Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the Council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. nigeria.description: The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured. The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety. The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety. “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.” Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms. He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. nigeria.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
nigeria.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. nigeria.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
nigeria.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. nigeria.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said. Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo. Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified. The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S. Vanguard News The post Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school appeared first on Vanguard News .

business.title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. business.title: Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. business.title: Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None Bitdeer sold every bitcoin it mined last week and still holds none of its own, the company said in its latest weekly update, continuing a nearly year-long strategy of turning production into cash after a weekend plunge in the bitcoin price. The Singapore-based miner reported output of 281.1 BTC and sales of 281.1 BTC for the week, for a net addition of zero. Its pure holdings, which exclude customer deposits, were zero as of Nov. 20. The sales came as bitcoin fell to a weekend low of $55,106 early Saturday at 1:17 AM ET, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The price has since bounced to near $62,700 as of 11:23 AM ET Monday. Bitdeer’s reserve has been drained all year Bitdeer’s treasury shrank from roughly 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025 to zero by Feb. 20, when Bitcoin Magazine reported the miner had liquidated its reserve over eight weeks. At the time, the company said the move should not be a concern for the broader market. Bitdeer’s filings show how little it has kept since. In its third-quarter results, filed with the SEC on a Form 6-K on Nov. 10, the company listed 47 BTC held at Sept. 30, down from 2,029 a year earlier. Its September production update showed 61 BTC held at the end of August. The company mined 1,355 BTC in September and 3,855 BTC in the third quarter, compared with 1,109 BTC in the same quarter of 2025. Self-mining margins stay thin Bitdeer has grown its fleet quickly. Self-mining hashrate reached 82.3 exahashes per second in the third quarter, up from 35.0 a year earlier, with another 28.7 exahashes per second of co-mining at third-party sites, the quarterly report shows . The economics are tight. Self-mining generated $217.5 million in revenue in the quarter but only $6.2 million in gross profit. Electricity averaged $47 per megawatt-hour, and the fleet ran at 15.4 joules per terahash. Bitdeer posted record revenue of $320.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $69.6 million, but a net loss of $125.5 million. That included a $54.6 million non-cash loss tied to a bitcoin-collateralized loan from a related party. Bitdeer also reported $213.7 million in cash and restricted cash, and its board authorized a new $100 million share repurchase program on Oct. 8. Borrowing against coins instead of selling them Not every miner is selling. American Bitcoin secured a $150 million revolving credit line from FalconX on Monday that is backed by its bitcoin. The company said the facility lets it raise cash without drawing down its reserve. The loan carries a 5.95% fee and an initial collateral ratio of 143%. Fully drawing it would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin. American Bitcoin has not said whether it has drawn on the line, and its release lists the risk that pledged coins could be liquidated if prices fall. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. sports.description: It turns out the man partially responsible for the beginning of Mike Norvell's downfall is set to become Florida State 's next football coach. Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann is expected to be named Florida State's next head football coach , USA TODAY Sports John Brice reported Monday, Nov. 23. The Glenn Schumann-coached Georgia defense coasted to a 63-3 win over the Seminoles in the 2023 Orange Bowl on Dec. 30, 2023. Just more that 1,000 days later, Schumann is set to replace Norvell, who was fired on Nov. 1. Schumann, 36, did not play college football, but enrolled at Alabama to work under legendary head coach Nick Saban in 2008. He worked in various roles under Saban and then-defensive coordinator Kirby Smart before following Smart to Athens, Georgia, as the inside linebackers coach in 2016. Schumann was promoted to co-defensive coordinator with now-Oregon coach Dan Lanning in 2019 and then served as co-defensive coordinator with Will Muschamp before being promoted to the full-time role in 2024, shortly after the blowout win vs. FSU. After the struggles Norvell had as a recruiter with the Seminoles , FSU fans may wonder about Schumann's experience and track record on the recruiting trail. Well, Schumann has helped the Bulldogs sign 14 five-stars during his time with the program. The relationship between Schumann and Wilson helped the Bulldogs pluck Wilson from Lincoln High School in Tallahassee to and send him to Athens instead of staying home with the Seminoles. Remember, at this time, FSU and Norvell were riding the high of coming off a 10-3 season. While Wilson is not the highest-ranked recruit Schumann added in his time at Georgia, he's been productive for the Bulldogs, tallying 102 career tackles, 8.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and an interception. Now the head coach at Florida State, keeping those relationships with Tallahassee-area programs will be key for Schumann. sports.title: Urban Meyer says Jeremiah Smith may be best college football player ever
sports.description: It's no surprise that former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer picked Ohio State to beat Michigan in the upcoming rivalry game on Nov. 28. While Meyer picked the Michigan defense as the best unit on the field, he had glowing words to say about Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. "On offense, we've got the best player in the country, maybe the best player ever to play college football. That's how good Jeremiah [Smith] is," Meyer said to 10TV . "But we also have a backup quarterback. And the offensive line's not playing great." Meyer predicted a low-scoring "rock fight" between the two likely non-playoff teams because of the strengths in Michigan's defense and Ohio State's offense. "I think this is going to be a rock fight, whoever punches the hardest is going to win" Urban Meyer says OSU has the more talented roster, but Michigan's defense is the best unit. "You've got to think: the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible ... they kept UCLA to three points until right near the end of the game, so that's a legit defense." Michigan upset UCLA with a 18-16 triple overtime victory on Nov. 21. Michigan's offense has been stagnant for most of the season, ranking 132nd in the FBS in yards per game and 129th in points per game. sports.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
sports.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. technology.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
technology.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®

science.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.

science.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
science.description:
Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast.
